Overview

The payment platform is being migrated from the legacy Oracle schema to PostgreSQL. Owner team: payment-team. Tracking epic: PAY-101.

Schedule

Original target cutover: 2026-10-15 (set in v3, 2026-09-20).

Revised target cutover: 2026-11-05 (v6, 2026-10-01) because of PAY-102 (schema incompatibility) and PAY-103 (authentication timeouts during staging validation).

Architecture

A dual-stack writer with a one-way backfill job (PAY-104) keeps the legacy and PostgreSQL stores consistent before the atomic cutover. Rollback procedure lives in CONF-PAY-002.

Related artefacts

Jira: PAY-101, PAY-102, PAY-103, PAY-104, PAY-105. Drive: GDRIVE-PAY-001, GDRIVE-PAY-002, GDRIVE-PAY-003. Slack: #payment-migration.

version.message: Revised cutover target from 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-05 after PAY-102 and PAY-103.

body.value:
Pre-cutover checklist

See PAY-105 for the cutover checklist. Freeze writes to the legacy schema 60 minutes before the window.

Rollback

Step 1: stop the dual-stack writer. Step 2: revert the application config flag. Step 3: replay the last 60 minutes of writes from the PostgreSQL change log. Added in v4 for the nullable-column incompatibility raised in PAY-102.

Known issues

Nullable-column divergence between legacy and PostgreSQL is tracked in PAY-102 and is not yet resolved. Authentication validation latency (PAY-103) must be green before the window opens.

Last reviewed

2026-09-28 by the payment-team.

version.message: Added rollback steps for the nullable-column incompatibility (PAY-102).

body.value:
Top risks

  1. Schema incompatibility (PAY-102) - high. Blocks the cutover. Mitigation: one-way backfill job PAY-104.
  2. Authentication validation latency (PAY-103, AUTH-201) - high. p99 of 4.2s on /validate observed in staging.
  3. Historical data backfill duration - medium. Estimated 14 hours.

Residual risk after mitigation

Medium. Recommend a second dry run before 2026-11-05.

version.message: Raised schema incompatibility to the top risk after PAY-102.

Day one

Request repository access through the engineering access form. Set up the local development environment using the bootstrap script in the platform repository.

Shared services

Authentication and session handling are provided by the auth service; see CONF-AUTH-001 for the current upgrade work.

Where to ask

#engineering on Slack for general questions, #payment-migration for payment platform work.

version.message: Added pointer to the authentication service upgrade.

body.value:
Goal

Move the authentication service from legacy session tokens to OAuth 2.1 with short-lived JWTs. Tracking issue: AUTH-201.

Workstreams

  • AUTH-202 - JWT signing key rotation (restricted details, security-team only).
  • AUTH-203 - deprecate legacy session tokens.
  • AUTH-204 - load test at 3x peak traffic.

Impact on other projects

Payment staging validation depends on the new validation path; see PAY-103.

Rollout

Feature-flagged rollout behind the auth-v2 flag, starting the sprint of 2026-09-28.

Milestones

  • 2026-09-28 - auth-v2 feature flag enabled in staging.
  • 2026-10-02 - legacy session token deprecation completed (AUTH-203).
  • 2026-10-03 - signing key rotation window (AUTH-202).
  • 2026-11-07 - fallback path removal.

Raw latency figures from the load test are in GDRIVE-AUTH-002.

version.message: Updated milestone dates after AUTH-203 completed.

Summary

A stale service account retained cluster-admin rights in the staging cluster and was used to escalate privileges on 2026-09-11. No production data was accessed.

Timeline

Detected 2026-09-11T22:40Z by an anomaly alert. Contained 2026-09-12T02:10Z. Postmortem held 2026-09-16.

Root cause

Offboarding workflow did not revoke cluster-scoped bindings for service accounts. Tracked as SEC-004.

Actions

  • SEC-005 - privileged access audit logging.
  • SEC-006 - contractor production access review.

Distribution

Security-team only. Do not forward outside this space.

version.message: Added the two follow-up actions (SEC-005, SEC-006).

body.value:
Scope

Review of all cluster-admin and production database bindings held in Q3 2026.

Findings

3 stale bindings found, 2 revoked, 1 pending vendor confirmation. The external contractor account (u007) holds read-only staging access only and was not implicated.

Compliance evidence

Exported for the compliance review; see GDRIVE-SEC-002.

Summary

Q4 2026 planning covers headcount, infrastructure and vendor spend. Forecast workbook: CONF-FIN-002 and GDRIVE-FIN-001.

Key movements

  • Infrastructure spend increases in Q4 for the authentication service upgrade (AUTH-201).
  • The payment migration delay moves approximately 40k of infrastructure spend from Q4 into Q1 2027.
  • Vendor spend restated by category after the compliance review.

Approvals

Pending leadership sign-off at the October review.

version.message: Restated vendor spend by category; shifted 40k infrastructure spend to Q1 2027.

Welcome

This handbook covers working hours, expenses, leave, and conduct expectations for all employees.

Leave

Annual leave entitlement is 25 days plus public holidays. Requests go through the HR system.

Expenses

Submit expenses within 30 days. Travel above 1000 requires manager approval.

Questions

Contact the HR team or post in #general.

version.message: Annual 2026 review; updated leave entitlement and expense window.

Employees may work remotely up to 3 days per week with manager approval. Fully remote arrangements require a documented exception.

Equipment

A one-time home office allowance is available. Contractors are covered by their agency agreement, not this policy.

Overview

This plan covers the analytics warehouse migration from Oracle to PostgreSQL, tracked as DP-301. It is the data platform workstream and is separate from the payment platform migration (PAY-101).

Scope

Event tables, reporting schemas and the batch ETL layer. Historical analytics events are backfilled under DP-302.

Status

In progress since 2026-09-08. No blockers currently.

Context

Retrospective for the 2025 identity provider migration, completed ahead of schedule with no customer impact.

What worked

  • Dual-run period of two weeks.
  • Cutover checklist rehearsed twice.

Lessons

Keep a named rollback owner in the runbook. Historical record only; unrelated to current projects.

Audience

Integration engineers onboarding new merchants to the existing payment platform.

Steps

  1. Collect merchant KYC documents.
  2. Provision sandbox credentials.
  3. Run test transactions.
  4. Enable production.

This covers merchant onboarding only and is not part of the platform migration (PAY-101).

Purpose

Company-wide information security policy covering access control, data classification and reporting obligations.

Access control

Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed quarterly.

Incidents

Suspected incidents are reported to the security team. Incident-specific records are handled under the incident response process and are not part of this policy document.

version.message: Annual review of the access control section.

Policy

All employees complete annual security awareness training. Enrollment for the 2026 program is tracked as SEC-007 and the slides are shared as GDRIVE-HR-002.

Compliance

Completion is reported to the compliance officer at quarter end.

Summary

Q3 2026 business review covering revenue, pipeline and headcount. The deck is GDRIVE-FIN-002.

Notes

The Q3 security incident is out of scope for this review and is handled separately by the security team. Q4 planning continues in CONF-FIN-001.
